findings: Rich fox reference plus neutral lighting improves material readability over the old simple toy references; current TRELLIS PBR still softens fine detail
First Hunyuan 2.1 fox output contains a large plane joined to the asset; it is not approved as a better default. Investigate via other subjects/seeds and preserve the failed visual evidence
mini fox tail geometry is coarse and facial proportions differ from reference; texture changes cannot fix these shape errors
Hunyuan 2.1 mechanical owl did not reproduce the fox floor artifact; the issue is subject/seed dependent and is not generalized to all outputs.

Complex ~1M-face assets require substantially more texture memory than simple toys. Observatory 1024 PBR reported 15642.93MiB allocated and 26706MiB reserved under Windows WDDM; this virtual allocator statistic is not a physical VRAM requirement or a low-VRAM guarantee.

UltraTex fox recovers quilted seams, metal engravings and white tail tip more faithfully than the initial TRELLIS texture; fur still appears glossy and geometric clumping remains. Fair same-mesh HDR comparison pending.
Hunyuan Paint initial fox result has view alignment/material-boundary artifacts despite a correct CUDA projection round trip; do not select it as a universal default merely because it runs

Neutral and HDR same-mesh comparisons favor UltraTex for fox seams and engraved detail; it can make owl enamel more metallic/teal than the reference. TRELLIS remains useful for lower-cost or more subdued materials.
